outcomes.text: Explain cloud concepts and the AWS value proposition
outcomes.observable: Given a business scenario, pick the cloud benefit, Well-Architected pillar, Cloud Adoption Framework perspective or migration strategy (the 7 Rs) that fits, and justify the choice in one sentence
For a stated latency, availability or data-residency requirement, choose between Regions, Availability Zones, edge locations, Local Zones, Wavelength and Outposts and name the reason

outcomes.text: Apply the shared responsibility model and AWS security services
outcomes.observable: Sort a list of security tasks into AWS versus customer responsibility for EC2, RDS and Lambda, and name the IAM feature or security service (GuardDuty, Shield, WAF, KMS, Inspector, Macie, CloudTrail, Config, Artifact) that answers a stated security or compliance need

outcomes.text: Identify the right AWS service for a requirement
outcomes.observable: Given a one-paragraph requirement, name the matching service across compute, storage, networking, database, integration, analytics, AI/ML, migration and management categories, and rule out the closest distractor

outcomes.text: Compare pricing models and choose cost and support resources
outcomes.observable: For a described workload, choose On-Demand, Reserved Instances, Savings Plans or Spot and estimate the relative saving; pick the right tool (Pricing Calculator, Budgets, Cost Explorer, Cost and Usage Report) and the cheapest Support plan that meets a stated response-time need

outcomes.text: Pass the CLF-C02 exam under exam conditions
outcomes.observable: Score at least 80% on two timed, full-length 65-question mock exams (90 minutes each) with every domain at or above 70%

out_of_scope.title: Hands-on console labs and deploying real workloads

out_of_scope.title: Associate-level architecture depth (subnet CIDR math, VPC routing design, database tuning)
out_of_scope.why: These belong to Solutions Architect Associate; the Cloud Practitioner exam only asks what each component is for
